Granted, I normally shoot a Glock 17 9mm but hear me out:

I'm not saying you can't use a .22lr for self defense. But it just has so little stopping power. This is just my opinion, but .380 is like the entry-level round for self defense.

If your main concern is "felt" recoil, the Bersa Thunder is an all-metal frame and weighs enough to mitigate much of the felt recoil. I would recommend against much smaller and lighter guns (like the Ruger LCP .380) as they are too light and you'll feel the recoil more. I can shoot my Glock all day, no problem. I can also shoot the Bersa Thunder .380 just fine. I can only fire a couple full magazines from the Ruger LCP .380 before I just don't want to shoot it anymore.

My other concern with .22lr handguns is reliability. Unless it's a revolver. Read through gun forums and .22's. If they're semi-automatic, they may have a propensity to be finicky about what ammo will work.

Just my $0.02, but I still think your wife would be better off with something bigger than .22lr for self defense and I think she could handle it just fine with proper training and the right firearm.
